topics: current stack: OpenAI + vLLM inference on prem for latency-sensitive features
compatibility: TGI model artifacts, kv cache, quantization
hosting modes: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-11 16:00 PST — duration ~55m; attendees listed above.

00:00:02 Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Lena, account exec at Redwood Inference. Marcus (our solutions engineer) and I will run through high level, understand your stack and blockers.
00:00:12 Priya Nair: hi, thanks. I'm Priya, CTO at Bluequarry. We run a hybrid setup today—OpenAI hosted endpoints for dev and some custom vLLM instances on-prem for latency-critical features.
00:00:27 Marcus Huang: cool, thanks. quick clarification, when you say vLLM, is that vLLM open-source on k8s or a managed service?
00:00:34 Tomás Rivera: it's self-hosted on k8s, some TGI adapters for a few models, we also experiment with quantized checkpoints.
00:00:42 Eliot Marsh: and infra wise we've got a private cloud in our colo plus AWS for burst workloads. security and data residency are the big drivers.

00:01:05 Lena Ortiz: got it. high-level we want to understand three things — compatibility with your existing artifacts (TGI format, kv cache exports), cost/latency targets, and security gating for private deploy. any immediate red lines?
00:01:20 Priya Nair: SOC2 compliance, must keep PII in our VPC for some endpoints. Also prefer bringing-your-own-kms for encryption.
00:01:30 Marcus Huang: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integration in private mode and we can surface audit logs — but we should walk through specifics. on compatibility: can you describe the artifacts you have for TGI?
00:01:44 Tomás Rivera: we have model folders that TGI serves, a couple Llama-family forks, and a few discriminator layers — also store kv-caches between requests for fast resumes. We push through vLLM in some jobs for batch.

00:02:12 Marcus Huang: okay, two threads — runtime compatibility and eval parity. runtime: we have a vLLM-compatible runtime layer on Redwood Dedicated/Private; most customers can reuse TGI artifacts with a small conversion step. sometimes tokenizer mismatches appear, and quantized checkpoints can require recompile.
00:02:30 Tomás Rivera: that tokenizer mismatch bit is a worry, we saw off-by-one tokenization differences when moving between vendor runtimes before.
00:02:37 Lena Ortiz: yep that's common. part of the pilot is to run an eval parity suite — same prompts, sampling seeds, and the same scoring heuristics. Marcus, do we have a mini-benchmark we can share?
00:02:46 Marcus Huang: I do — we’ll send a mini-benchmark script that runs your prompt set against Redwood Hosted, our Dedicated pool, and a Private node (if you want to try). it reports latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, and exact-match/regression on your scoring.

00:03:10 Priya Nair: what's the typical overhead moving from vLLM to Redwood runtime? Any code changes in model serving?
00:03:17 Marcus Huang: most customers need 0-2 small changes: tokenizers, an optional kv cache export/import shim, and sometimes a quantization profile update. If you're using TGI wrappers we usually have compatibility layers. For large models quantized to int4/int8 we recommend specific kernel choices — we can propose those after we see the artifacts.

00:03:45 Eliot Marsh: on private deployment, how do upgrades and rollouts look? we can't afford a broad regression that impacts customers.
00:03:52 Marcus Huang: we support canary rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback to pinned model versions. Dedicated has controlled upgrade windows and Private (VPC) can be managed by our control plane while the data plane stays in your network.

00:04:20 Tomás Rivera: cost wise, we're comparing token pricing from OpenAI for hosted and our own infra opex. curious about Redwood's unit economics—how do batching and KV cache reduce cost?
00:04:32 Lena Ortiz: Redwood Optimize surfaces batching and cache suggestions; with KV caching and continuous batching you often see 20-60% per-token cost reductions for conversational flows. We can run a cost projection once we have traffic profiles.

00:05:05 Priya Nair: earlier you mentioned fallback to cheaper variants — can we route by policy? e.g., low-latency traffic goes to dedicated nodes, lower priority goes to hosted cheap variant.
00:05:13 Marcus Huang: yes, smart routing policies support latency/cost/region tiers. You can define rules per route. We'll show a routing example in the follow-up doc.

00:05:40 Eliot Marsh: network — how does the Private deployment connect to our VPC? do we need a VPN or private link?
00:05:46 Lena Ortiz: both supported. we have partner integrations and can use PrivateLink, Direct Connect, or customer-managed VPN. we also support air-gapped on-prem packages if needed.

00:06:12 Tomás Rivera: Prompts — we rely on streaming partial tokens for progressive UI. Does Redwood support streaming and function calling?
00:06:18 Marcus Huang: yes to streaming. function-calling patterns work similarly to the OpenAI spec; we also support structured outputs and tools. occasional differences in chunking exist but we keep streaming low-latency.

00:06:40 Priya Nair: let's talk about eval parity specifics — what failure modes do you see in migrations?
00:06:48 Marcus Huang: typical failures: tokenization drift, subtle sampling differences, quantization regressions (hallucination increase), and prompt contextual windows mismatch. We mitigate with seed alignment, same sampling params, and targeted calibration runs.
00:07:05 Tomás Rivera: can we pin model versions? we need reproducible outputs for audits.
00:07:09 Lena Ortiz: absolutely, model pinning and rollout policies are first-class.

00:07:30 Eliot Marsh: security — audit logs, who has access, SSO?
00:07:36 Marcus Huang: RBAC, SSO/SAML, and per-token tracing in the console. For Private we can route logs to your SIEM.

00:08:05 Priya Nair: data retention — we need confirmation that prompts and outputs are not stored by hosted provider for certain routes.
00:08:12 Lena Ortiz: Hosted API has configurable retention; enterprise tiers and Dedicated can be configured not to persist logs. Private ensures data never leaves your network. We'll include explicit retention settings in the security doc.

00:08:40 Tomás Rivera: any known issues with TGI adapters? we run some custom handler code.
00:08:47 Marcus Huang: custom handlers usually work but we recommend extracting the minimal transform into a shim. if the adapter is Python-based we can containerize and run it in Private/Dedicated.

00:09:20 Priya Nair: timeline — we're evaluating now, pilot next quarter. our success criteria: parity on 10 core prompts, <80ms P50 latency for user-facing path, and clear encryption/KMS controls.
00:09:32 Lena Ortiz: understood. that sounds reasonable. Marcus, we'll propose a pilot plan.

00:09:45 Marcus Huang: proposed pilot: 2 weeks of artifact ingestion and conversion, run 10k prompt evals across Hosted and a Dedicated node, measure P50/P95 and regression on scoring. if parity within tolerance, expand to Private deployment runway.

00:10:12 Eliot Marsh: curious about autoscaling — do you support burst to cloud if private pool saturated?
00:10:18 Marcus Huang: yes, hybrid routing with fallback to Dedicated/Hosted is supported, subject to policy and data residency rules. for PII-bound routes we'd keep in private; for stateless or public data we can burst.

00:10:45 Priya Nair: ok, can you walk me through an example conversion flow — say a TGI model artifact with quantized weights?
00:10:53 Marcus Huang: in brief: ingest the artifact, validate tokenizer and vocab, run a quantization profile check (int8/int4), recompile kernels for our runtime, run a smoke eval. If tokenizer mismatch occurs we provide a shim or regenerate tokenizers. sometimes re-quantizing with our profile avoids regressions.

00:11:30 Tomás Rivera: any examples of regressions after re-quantization?
00:11:35 Marcus Huang: yes, hallucination rate upticks have occurred when quantization was aggressive without calibration. our Optimize toolkit recommends quant profiles per workload; we also surface regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

00:12:02 Priya Nair: do you expose token-level cost in console? We want per-route cost attribution.
00:12:08 Lena Ortiz: yes, per-token cost breakdown, per-route and per-model dashboards with token attribution.

00:12:35 Eliot Marsh: SLA — what's your uptime and latency commitments for Dedicated?
00:12:40 Lena Ortiz: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include exact numbers in the follow-up SOW.

00:12:55 Marcus Huang: quick note: sometimes transcriptions of kernels and lib versions matter — we'll capture runtime env and kernel selection in the artifact ingest report so you can audit it.

00:13:20 Tomás Rivera: do you integrate with our existing CI/CD for model rollouts?
00:13:25 Marcus Huang: yes, we have APIs and webhook events for rollout pipelines and we can plug into your CI to automate promotion from canary to prod.

00:13:50 Priya Nair: ok let's surface risks — I'm worried about tokenization drift and quantization regressions.
00:13:57 Marcus Huang: we'll mitigate with seed alignment runs, calibrations, and if needed keep your vLLM for the most sensitive paths while we ramp Redwood for others.

00:14:20 Lena Ortiz: commercial — any procurement constraints? purchase order? multi-year?
00:14:26 Eliot Marsh: procurement will want enterprise contract with data residency clauses and a support SLA. we prefer annual reserved capacity if costs align.

00:14:40 Lena Ortiz: noted. for Dedicated we can do reserved capacity with burst options. for Private there is a platform fee + support. I'll include pricing bands in the follow-up.

00:15:10 Tomás Rivera: curious about network egress for hosting — token charges—do you have bandwidth concerns?
00:15:17 Marcus Huang: network egress depends on where the data plane runs. for Hosted you'll see standard egress; for Private/VPC it's in your network so you control egress.

00:15:40 Priya Nair: let's talk sample prompt flow — we'll send 10 core prompts plus 3 longer contexts. can you ensure the benchmark script supports streaming and exact-match scoring?
00:15:49 Marcus Huang: yes we'll adapt the script to your scoring functions. We'll also capture n-gram overlap and custom metrics you provide.

00:16:20 Eliot Marsh: internal stakeholders — security, legal, infra, ML. procurement timeline ~4-6 weeks after pilot.

00:16:35 Lena Ortiz: next steps recap: I'll send SOC2 + network diagram; Marcus will send benchmark kit; Tomás will send prompt set; schedule a technical deep dive for private deployment with Eliot next week.

00:16:55 Priya Nair: sounds good. any other questions?
00:17:00 Tomás Rivera: one more — how do you handle model lineage and auditability for regulated requests?
00:17:07 Marcus Huang: we include model lineage metadata in logs and the console; Private can persist lineage internally. we can export audit trails to your SIEM.

00:17:35 Priya Nair: okay thanks, that's helpful.

00:17:40 Lena Ortiz: great. we'll follow up with the docs. thanks everyone.

00:18:02 Meeting ended per recording. Note: transcript quality medium — occasional mis-transcription of proper nouns (TGI/TJ?), Spanish accents on Tomas' name sometimes garbled.

00:18:30 Appendix: references mentioned — security snapshot (to be sent), benchmark script (to be sent), pilot SOW sketch (to be shared).
